Script.name: GUI Lifecycle
Script.script:
-- ============================================================================= -- ENTRY POINT HANDLERS -- These ensure GUI.initializeOrRefresh is called at the right times -- while preserving other initialization functions -- =============================================================================
-- The onProtocolEnabled handler is defined in the MSDP script section -- It handles MSDP variable registration and GUI initialization
-- The main initialization handlers are registered at the bottom of this script -- along with the original GUI.init() registration to ensure proper order
-- Since Mudlet 4.20, sysLoadEvent passes a boolean: true for a fresh profile -- load, false when it fires after resetProfile(). That distinction matters: -- after a resetProfile() the connection is usually still up and MSDP was -- already negotiated, so sysProtocolEnabled will NOT fire again and the GUI -- would otherwise sit empty, never having sent its REPORT subscriptions. function GUI.onSysLoadEvent(_, isNewLoad) GUI.debug("LIFECYCLE", "sysLoadEvent fired", { isNewLoad = isNewLoad, initializedBefore = GUI.initialized, }) GUI.init() if type(GUI.debugSnapshot) == "function" then GUI.debugCall( "SNAPSHOT/sysLoad immediate", GUI.debugSnapshot, "sysLoadEvent immediate" ) tempTimer(2, GUI.debugWrap("LIFECYCLE/sysLoad delayed snapshot", function() GUI.debugCall( "SNAPSHOT/sysLoad delayed", GUI.debugSnapshot, "sysLoadEvent plus two seconds" ) end)) end
-- isNewLoad == false means we came from resetProfile(). Older Mudlet -- versions pass nil here, so only take this path on an explicit false. if isNewLoad == false then tempTimer(0.5, GUI.debugWrap("LIFECYCLE/profile reset recovery", function() if map and map.initialize then local ok, initialized = GUI.debugCall( "LIFECYCLE/profile reset/map.initialize", map.initialize ) if not ok or initialized == false then print("[GUI] Mapper initialization failed after profile reset: " .. tostring(initialized)) end else print("[GUI] Mapper initialization is unavailable after profile reset") end if GUI.requestMSDPReports() then print("[GUI] Re-subscribed to MSDP after profile reset") end GUI.initializeOrRefresh("profile reset") end)) end end
function GUI.onConnectionEvent(...) GUI.debug("LIFECYCLE", "sysConnectionEvent fired", {...}) tempTimer(1, GUI.debugWrap("LIFECYCLE/connection refresh timer", function() GUI.initializeOrRefresh("connection established") if type(GUI.debugSnapshot) == "function" then GUI.debugCall( "SNAPSHOT/connection", GUI.debugSnapshot, "one second after connection" ) end end)) end
-- Keep lifecycle registration idempotent when scripts are recompiled or a -- fixed release is upgraded again in the same Mudlet session. The legacy -- anonymous closures from pre-split releases did not expose IDs; the guarded -- GUI entry points above coalesce their one unavoidable migration overlap. GUI.lifecycleHandlerIds = GUI.lifecycleHandlerIds or {} local function registerLifecycleHandler(event, handler) local previousId = GUI.lifecycleHandlerIds[event] if previousId then pcall(killAnonymousEventHandler, previousId) GUI.lifecycleHandlerIds[event] = nil end
local ok, handlerId = pcall(registerAnonymousEventHandler, event, handler) if ok then GUI.lifecycleHandlerIds[event] = handlerId else GUI.debugError( "LIFECYCLE/register/" .. event, "failed to register " .. tostring(handler) .. ": " .. tostring(handlerId) ) end end
registerLifecycleHandler("sysLoadEvent", "GUI.onSysLoadEvent") registerLifecycleHandler("sysInstall", "GUI.init")
-- Register protocol handler early to ensure it catches MSDP enablement -- This is critical because MSDP can be enabled before GUI.init() completes registerLifecycleHandler("sysProtocolEnabled", "GUI.onProtocolEnabled")
-- Add connection-based refresh registerLifecycleHandler("sysConnectionEvent", "GUI.onConnectionEvent")
